utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Good afternoon. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-95-13/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Mile Mrksic and Miroslav Radic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mrksic, good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MRKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you follow what I am saying in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MRKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Please take a chair. Mr. Radic, good afternoon to you, too. Do I take it that you can follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED RADIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Please state the appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Jan Wubben, senior trial attorney. Together with me is attorney Mark McKeon and Ms. Kristina Carey and David Bruff as case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And good afternoon to you all. Appearances for Mr. Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. For Mr. Mrksic, it's Mr. Miroslav Vasic, attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good afternoon to you. And appearances for Mr. Radic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Borivoje Borovic, the attorney for Miroslav Radic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, thank you. And good afternoon to you, too. So welcome. This is a Status Conference that is being convened this time with two of the co-accused under this indictment present. I will inform you about further developments that are expected in this trial with regard to the third person who has actually arrived here in The Hague, Mr. Sljivancanin and whose initial appearance will be tomorrow at 3.30. The last Status Conference was convened on the 5th of March of this year, and as you may imagine, it was only Mr. Mrksic present, together with his counsel. Mr. Radic had not yet been taken into custody at the time. And so this is the first time that Mr. Radic is having a Status Conference. The initial appearance of Mr. Radic took place, as you all remember, on the 21st of May of this year. And I will repeat just for your sake, Mr. Radic, what I have stated and told Mr. Mrksic on previous occasions, is that our Rules and Rule 65 bis requires me, as the Pre-Trial Judge, to summon to all a Status Conference within 120 days after the last Status Conference. So in other words, Mr. Mrksic has his Status Conference today, within the 120-day period. In your case, and again in the case of Mr. Mrksic, you will have another Status Conference within another 120 days to be reckoned from today. And the purpose behind this provision under our Rules is a very practical and useful one. Mr. Mrksic, obviously, has heard this before. But Mr. Radic hasn't, and so I will repeat what the raison d'etre of the Status Conference is for your sake. The idea is to have these periodical interconferences for two or three mains purposes. The first one is to organise and establish exchanges between the parties, with a view to ensuring an expeditious preparation of the trial. And I can assure you that that is on my mind, and also on the mind of the other two Judges that constitute together with me Trial Chamber II. We are doing our level best to chase matters up so that the trial can start without any undue delay. And the second, and perhaps extremely important reason for holding such conferences is to give you the opportunity, Mr. Mrksic and Mr. Radic personally or through your counsel to raise issues relating to your detention here in Scheveningen and in The Hague, and also in relation to your mental and physical conditions. And I can assure you that you can speak frankly here, and that you will suffer absolutely no consequences at all for any grievance or complaint that you may have and air here. I am informed by my senior legal officer that in preparation for this Status Conference, he held under my direction a Rule 65 ter meeting with the Office of the Prosecutor and the Defence counsel for both accused. And this was held on the 30th of June. That's a couple of days ago. I am also informed by Mr. Von Hebel that as a result of this Rule 65 ter meeting, there is no need for me as a Pre-Trial Judge or for the pre-trial Chamber to go into certain matters which were dealt with during the Status Conference on which there is agreement and consensus. There are, however, some outstanding matters that today we will go straight into. You will recall, although Mr. -- I did mention this during the initial appearance of Mr. Radic, too, you will recall that we are still operating under an indictment that goes back in years and includes the name also of another co-accused at the time that is no longer amongst the living. And that before the arrival of Mr. Radic here, the indictment against Mr. Mrksic had undergone some amendments, while Mr. Radic was arraigned here on the basis of the original indictment. There was at the time already expectations of the arrival of the third person, Mr. Sljivancanin, and there is no doubt that at the present moment, there is an absolute need for the indictment to be amended and updated. I know through Mr. Von Hebel that it was raised during the 65 ter meeting he had with you, and that he has emphasised with you that it is imperative if we are not to undergo undue delays, unnecessary delays, it is necessary that the amended indictment is filed before the end of this month. And I have been given the date of the 21st of July of this year as the deadline, which you should observe. And that is in accordance with a previous decision that we took. So do I take it, Mr. Wubben - forgive me if I don't pronounce your name well, correctly - do I take it we shall have an amended indictment by the 21st of July?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We start drafting it and we will be ready at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As I told you a few minutes ago, Mr. Sljivancanin has arrived here. And tomorrow, there will be his initial appearance. And I take it that he will be arraigned as well, like Mr. Radic, on the basis of the old indictment. So what my suggestion to you, and I know that you probably are operating along these lines already, is to ensure that any amendment to the indictment would incorporate Mr. Sljivancanin because, as I pointed out during the last Status Conference, there is already a decision of Trial Chamber II that for all intents and purposes, the three persons I mentioned, Mr. Sljivancanin, Mr. Radic, Mr. Mrksic, will be tried together, the same trial as codefendants. So the indictment needs to be amended accordingly so as not to have to go through the exercise again after the arraignment of Mr. Sljivancanin. In other words, he will be then served with another copy of the indictment as amended, and we can take it then from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I can confirm that we will file a new consolidated indictment against those three accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. That's perfect. Mr. Radic, you have filed a motion for provisional release. The Prosecution has promised us to file a response, we are expecting that response. As soon as it arrives, you will have an opportunity, if you want, to present further comments. But it is already on the agenda of Trial Chamber II, which basically means that we have already made preparations, Judge Schomburg, myself, and Judge Mumba, to give your motion for provisional release all due consideration. And we promise you that we will proceed with handing down a decision at our earliest. This is to put your mind at rest that your motion is receiving attention. But we are at the moment awaiting the response from the Prosecution. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we filed today -- we filed our response today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Which basically -- thank you, Mr. Wubben. Which basically means -- have you received a copy of it? Not yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let me suggest the following. I will be approaching at the end of today's hearing Judge Schomburg so that we tie up, together with Judge Mumba, and start deliberating on this. In the meantime, once you have been served with a copy, if you have further comments, I suggest that you file them not later than Wednesday of next week, of this coming week. That should put us in a position to decide without any undue delay. You are aware, I suppose, that we have already handed down a decision, Mr. Borovic, with regard to your motion Defence preliminary motion with regard to the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, we have been informed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And once you have heard me express myself on the need to have the indictment in general, then you would understand why what is your motion, because it would have been a preemptive measure to deal with it otherwise. There is a Defence request on the part of Mr. Mrksic for to this Chamber to rule for communicating on the -- on the rules for communicating with potential witnesses. You will recall that we decided this matter earlier on in this year against the motion. You requested certification, which we granted, and the matter is still pending before the Appeals Chamber. Naturally, we will await the outcome of the decision of the Appeals Chamber before we can take this matter any further. And for the time being, everything will stay put pending that decision. I know that in the course of the 65 ter meeting that you had with Mr. Von Hebel, you discussed also disclosure matters in terms of Rule 66, the various parts of Rule 66. I am informed, and I want a confirmation from you, that you have agreed that this 66(A)(i) material has already been disclosed to the Defence counsel, to both parties; that's both Mr. Mrksic and Mr. Radic. Confirmed?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We did receive supporting material pursuant to this Rule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: May I suggest, Mr. Wubben, to prepare the same bundle for the newcomer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: It's already prepared, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would have imagined so. There was a matter which -- on which there seemed to be an absence Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of an agreement in the course of the 65 ter meeting regard to disclosures under Rule 66(A)(ii). But I understand that you are moving in the direction of disclosing this material, too. I understand that you were finding an objection to disclosing it pending the conclusion of the interview with accused Radic. I take it that you have changed course now and you are going to stick to what is provided by that provision of our Rules and proceed with the disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, let me first confirm that we already abide with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence according to disclosure. But in the previous stage, we had an agreement and discussions with counsel for Mrksic on disclosure. We had even a written agreement on it. But now there's new circumstances. The preliminary motion dealt with by Trial Chamber, an appeal, and a new accused arrived in the meantime and one to come, so there was also discussion at the 65 ter meeting. There were requests and wishes for disclosure policy, and I can now confirm to you that the OTP proposed to both counsel to start the disclosure by filing a substantial package with a view to Rule 68 disclosure to counsels. I informed counsels of it. We will start this package this month, transferring it to counsels. We even will seek the possibility and discuss that with counsels for filing via CD-ROM. That will be then easier according to the volume of it, and that will be then a start of a subsequent step and making steps of further disclosing various packages of disclosing material all in accordance with and in discussion and agreement with counsels. And we will keep contact with counsel during that period. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben. But I was particularly referring to the disclosure of the statements of those witnesses the Prosecution intends to call. And I understand that you had raised an objection you would consider it inappropriate to disclose now, at this juncture, the statements of those witnesses you seek to call at the trial, particularly since the interview with the accused Radic was still pending. And it was put to you that this -- although it may well be a preference, it's not the preference that can fall or have the blessing of Rule 66(A)(ii) and that you need to proceed with the disclosure. Do I have your word and your commitment that you are proceeding with the disclosure of these statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The package will include also the Rule 66(A)(ii) material, though we - and that was the clarification I confirmed at the 65 ter meeting - we have not yet determined our witnesses so far. But the statements we will send, including in the package, are, of course, potential witnesses for us as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Are you happy with that, Mr. Vasic and Mr. Borovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would just like to speak in reaction to the words of my colleague pursuant to Rule 68, and that would be that I would accept this option, that most of the package we could receive starting the beginning of this month. As far as Rule 66(A)(ii) is concerned, if these statements are part of the package, then the Defence will agree to that. I would just like to remind that it would be good and expeditious for the preparation of the Defence if the Prosecutor can forward this material to us in a timely fashion, at least in relation to the witnesses that he is certain will appear. And considering that a whole trial has already been heard here before this Tribunal, it would be good to know which witnesses will be appearing here for this case. And that will certainly help the Defence to prepare our evidence and our witnesses and to be ready for the trial. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have had discussions, individual discussion, with Mr. Wubben in preparation for this Status Conference in relation to the material pursuant to Rule 68, and the agreement was that the materials would be handed over to us by the end of July, that is within three weeks, that is what we agreed today. So not the beginning of the month, but that will be either through the CD-ROM or the material will be copied and sent to the Defence team members. As far as 66(A)(ii), if the material and documents include -- 68 are included, then that will be good. Your Honour, you have also mentioned that in their submission, the Prosecution said that Mr. Radic will be giving an interview. Now, we are ready in spite of all the dangers that could be threatening an accused, considering that the indictment is in preparation to be amended. At the moment when we had to make a decision, when Mr. Radic's father died, we were then ready to proceed in this direction. However, at this moment, we don't know what the indictment will look like, that is, the joint consolidated indictment with the three accused will look like. So that means that the acts can be completely differently described in the new indictment. If that is so, then once that is issued and confirmed, we will have different situations in relation to the interview. As far as the material pursuant to Rule 68 is concerned, it is certain, regardless of the indictment that is to come, I think the Prosecution can start with disclosure of this material because that is something that the accused could certainly use now. As far as the Rule 66(A)(ii) is concerned, the materials pursuant to this Rule, we haven't heard from Mr. Wubben when this material will be disclosed to us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So the position, Mr. Wubben, I'm addressing you in particular at this point, seems to be the following: I take it from the information that I have with regard to Rule 68 that I had mentioned myself but was raised by Mr. -- both by yourself and Mr. Vasic and Mr. Borovic, that I do appreciate that observing Rule 68 most of the time in most trials proves to be an ongoing process. My duty at the present moment is to remind you that you have a responsibility under Rule 68 to disclose to the Defence all exculpatory material that you may be aware of at the present moment. The indication that I have is that you intend to do so, so I will not proceed any further and say anything more. I will leave it in your hands to confirm to what is provided under Rule 68. Only thing that will need to be done, if you are not happy with the way the disclosure is taking place under Rule 68, then it is your, in your interest, to bring the matter to the attention of the -- of myself as a Pre-Trial Judge. But I have no reason, basing myself on past experience in this Tribunal, to doubt for a minute that the Prosecution will try to avoid complying with this Rule 68. I do realise that there may be problems trying to disclose all the material at the same time and within a very short time. But I'm pretty sure that you will do your best. With regard to 66(A)(ii), the only concession that I make, Mr. Wubben, is that due to the fact that the indictment is going to be -- undergo some amendments, this may, indeed, reflect on the number and the identities of the witnesses that you might want to bring forward. And this is the only concession that I am making. However, I am pretty sure that since this is an indictment that goes back in years, and events which were amongst the very first to be investigated by this Tribunal, that you are certainly in a position to be a hundred per cent sure about the great majority of the witnesses that will be brought forward, will be produced in this case. So I'm going -- not going to make an order today. But I am specifically inviting you to disclose the statements of the witnesses that you absolutely have no reason to doubt retaining as witnesses in this case. And I expect those to be in the great majority, as I said. And the disclosure has got absolutely nothing to do with any interview you may or may not have with Mr. Radic. All right. Point taken?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Point taken and accepted. Just clarifying to you as well that from this very moment, we cannot provide all the 66(A)(ii) witnesses. We have also, of course, to do the searching and the translations. But as I confirmed, this is an ongoing subsequent step.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And there is one final matter that was raised in the course of the 65 ter meeting, and that is about reciprocal disclosure. And I take it that you still maintain that you are not in a position to inform the Trial Chamber -- me, as the Pre-Trial Judge, whether you will trigger off this process. Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. Mr. Mrksic's Defence is not in the position to say anything about this because we have not received a final text of the indictment, or the material that we expect from our learned friends. Once we receive all these materials, the Defence is going to consider this issue and will inform you in due time, Your Honours. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is our joint position. Once we receive the consolidated indictment and the materials according to this Rule, we will be able to give you our position. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So is there anything else you would like to raise with regard to the matters of disclosure?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, thank you. Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If at any moment you're not happy with the process, the whole process of disclosure, please bring it to my attention. The next matter to be discussed obviously is on the one of which I can say very little, and that is the date of the trial. I repeat that tomorrow there will be the initial appearance of Mr. Sljivancanin. As from that moment, he will be joined together with the two other accused that we have here today. There will be, of course, the new amended indictment. There will be pleas. We are still at the very early stages of this whole process, very much depends on how things go on, what pleas we will have, including any possible plea of guilty that you may -- I don't know, but it's not to be ruled out. You may give it a thought as well. And I cannot at the present moment give you an indication of when this trial can start. Depends on when other trials will finish, and it also depends on how we go along in the pre-trial stage. And you all have a part to play in this whole process. The more you prolong the proceedings, obviously the more -- the longer the proceedings will take. And my invitation to you is to remember that it's in everybody's interest, but particularly in the interest of your two clients, to have this trial started at the earliest possible opportunity. Having said that, is there any other matter that you would like to raise? Yes, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe we can discuss the following at the Status Conference: The Defence would kindly ask the Chamber to submit to the Defence all the materials which are not confidential or which were not heard ex parte, so all the judicial decisions, statements, that is not confidential.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand what you mean. All the materials which are not confidential or which were not heard ex parte, all judicial decisions, statements that are not confidential. In this case, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this has not been translated well. All the motions that we have sent either to the Prosecution or to the Chamber, all the court rulings which have not been submitted to the Defence, and not confidential or have not been sent ex parte, if the Chamber is able, can the Chamber send to the Defence of Mr. Radic? Anything that concerns the trial so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I see absolutely no problem, but what surprises me is that you are not in possession of all the motions. Do you refer also to the motions which were filed and decisions taken prior to the arrival of your client here? Is this what you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean all the rulings, all decisions, all the motions that are relative to this case and will have a bearing on the position of Mr. Radic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I take it that what is being requested, Mr. Von Hebel, and there absolutely shouldn't be any problem -- in fact I'm not even consulting the Prosecution on this -- all the documentation consisting of motions and all other filings, and that includes also decisions, both oral and in writing, of this Trial Chamber, and of myself as Pre-Trial Judge given in this case are to be copied and given to Mr. Borovic. Mr. Borovic, those which are only in the English language, do we need to have them translated? You would spare the Tribunal a lot of expenses and a lot of time and resources if you can accept them in the English language in which they probably are.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will save the Tribunal both the money and the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Borovic. So you will take care of, Mr. Von Hebel. I thank you. Anything else you would like to raise? Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you. Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the Rules require me now to inquire from each of the accused whether they would like to raise any matter related to their state of health and their condition of detention. I'll start with Mr. Mrksic. Mr. Mrksic, the Rules -- you've heard what I said. The Rules require me to inquire from you whether you have anything to state, whether you would like to make a statement with regard to your state of health and state of detention. Do you have reasons to complain about anything? Are you receiving all the attention that you require, given your health condition?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MRKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, last time, at the last Status Conference, I gave you all the details about my problem. You have extended me all the support. I am undergoing medical checkups. I am receiving an increased amount of medication every day. But apart from that, I have no other objections. So much from me. I thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Mrksic. Please take a chair. Mr. Radic. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED RADIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the time being, I have no health problems. As far as the conditions in the Detention Unit, I have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. If at any time -- if at any time between now and when we have the next Status Conference you have any problem related to your health or to the conditions of your detention in the Detention Unit in Scheveningen, please feel free to bring them to my notice, and I promise you I will act and give the matter my utmost attention. All right. Having said that, I think, unless you would like to raise any other matter, I can close this Status Conference, advising you that the next one will be held within the 120 days that is provided for under Rule 65 bis. And the next Status Conference we will have present the third accused. Thank you. And good afternoon to you all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: adjourned at 3.47 p.m.
